issues.area: C2 / S3-R25 item 3 inventory: deferBehindVerdict costs O(E) per join (new probe)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFollow.swift:964-978. deferBehindVerdict scans eventsAfterFollow with lastIndex, then inserts into eventsAfterFollow and eventStamps right after the verdict. It is called once per moved id from Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineJobs.swift:117-121 (addInterest, in a follow visit, when the target's attemptEnd.deferredAfter is set). The draft's row (docs/adr-drafts/s3f.md:4850) reads 'no figure: put to the orchestrator'.
issues.problem:
PROBE-C20R-DEFER-BEHIND-C2 is at .build-orchestrator/s3f-probes-c20/reqs/VerifyC20ReqsC2Probes.swift (release, -enable-testing). Its shape:
- 10,000 prefetch members share H.
- O is a user job, held and then answered with a 404, so its verdict waits behind v3's owed follow.
- v4 then maps every member to O.

H's bounded visit moves 512 ids a turn onto O, and each join is deferred behind O's waiting verdict. A turn's cost grows with E, the number of waiting events: '#15=34.29 ms (E 8705)', '#16=36.29 ms (E 9217)', '#17=38.13 ms (E 9729)'.

The longest held turn, best of 3, in three samples:
- 37.91 ms at 04:58, load 4.49 to 4.69, while my TSan run was still on the host;
- 35.78 ms at 05:20:53 to 05:20:59, load { 1.42 2.85 46.86 } to { 1.51 2.82 46.34 };
- 36.52 ms at 05:23:17 to 05:23:25, load { 1.96 2.57 39.86 } to { 1.88 2.53 39.41 }.

The heartbeat agrees with the held-turn timer. Every sample is 3.6 to 3.8 times c2Budget at a 1-minute load of 10 or less, which makes the row blocking under S3-R25 item 3.

The probe reached its shape: 'verdictWaited true', maxE 9729, and 9,489 joins still waited after the follow's last turn ran the drain's first batch of 511. The probe's own '>= 10,000' setup check was too strict; it is the only other issue the probe records.

The fixer's concentrationNotFoundTurns (6.66 ms) does not cover this case, because there the ids converge before the verdict waits.
issues.fix: Make the deferral O(1) amortised. For example, keep the joins deferred behind a waiting verdict, with their stamps, in a side list keyed by (target, epoch), and have the drain replay that list right after the verdict's own replay. That removes the per-join lastIndex scan and both mid-array inserts. Keep today's replay order, or record any order change under S3-R16 item 2; no answer may change. Pin the probe's shape as a BenchSync release case at best of 3 <= c2Budget. Add a deterministic test in both orders that the drain replays the deferred joins after the verdict with the visit-first answers, and kill the side list's drop-mutant 2/2. Then fill in the inventory row.

issues.problem:
PROBE-C20C-MANY-MOVES proves it (release, -enable-testing, 05:09:53-05:09:59, load {3.45 5.71 97.60} -> {3.58 5.69 97.06}).
- Shape: H is 10,000 prefetch members sharing one content (one job, download held). k user publications are held at their first store unit. v3 maps k of H's members, one each, onto the publications' contents while the follow is held, so H is not visited. v4 is applied while the follow is owed. Its `bringInboundOntoPublications` walk records one move off H per publication (owed after v4 = k, all off H). The next follow turn's `continueInbound` then makes all k moves.
- k=1: [8.36, 8.43, 8.22] ms, best 8.22.
- k=16: [79.55, 82.77, 79.95] ms, best 79.55 (thread CPU 79.52).
- k=64: [305.56, 305.45, 304.79] ms, best 304.79 (thread CPU 304.79).
- The turn that follows each of these takes about 1.3 ms. Each move of one id costs about 4.7 ms, which is an O(N log N) sort plus O(N) copy-on-write copies of H's 10,000 ids.
- `budget.holders` allows 256 such moves in a turn, so a turn can reach more than 1 s.
- The draft's inventory row reads "<= 10,000 ids a turn over the holders". That is wrong: the same holder's ids are re-sorted for every move. The row has no figure, so S3-R25 item 3 makes it blocking.
- No answer or invariant differed (violations []).
